cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). He's just finished teaching how the church should pray and worship together (1 Timothy 2:1-15). Now he hands Timothy a trustworthy saying about anyone who aspires to be an overseer in the church.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who aspires to be an overseer desires a noble task.

cards.text: Then Paul starts a LIST, friend. An overseer must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled and respectable.

cards.question: Paul's list keeps going. He says an overseer of the church must be hospitable and able to teach.

cards.text: An overseer must not be dependent on wine, and not violent but gentle and peaceable. I once yelled at an oven timer for a FULL minute, so I'm reading this one twice.

cards.question: An overseer must be gentle and peaceable. What else must he be free of?

cards.text: Next, an overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity. Friend, I had six little cutters on one counter, and catching them before they wobbled off the edge was a FULL-TIME job.

cards.question: Why does it matter so much how an overseer runs his own household?

answers.text: It shows if he can care for God's church
His family will help him lead the church
The church will gather in his house

cards.text: Then Paul says an overseer must not be a recent convert. And Paul spells out exactly how that could go sideways.

cards.question: Paul warns that a recent convert put in charge may become ___ and fall under condemnation.

cards.text: Last item for overseers: he must have a good reputation with outsiders. Paul's not just checking references at church, friend; he's calling the NEIGHBORS.

cards.question: Why does an overseer need a good reputation with people outside the church?

answers.text: So he won't fall into disgrace and the devil's snare
So more outsiders will want to join the church
So the city's rulers will protect the church

cards.text: Now Paul turns to deacons. They must be dignified and not double-tongued, so NO telling somebody "Love the cookies!" and then roasting them in the group chat.

cards.question: Deacons must not be given to much wine or greedy for ___.

cards.text: Deacons must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience. But you don't hand a brand new oven the BIG order until it proves itself, and Paul doesn't hand deacons the job that way either.

cards.question: Before anyone serves as a deacon, they must first be ___.

cards.text: Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons. That oven passed the test batch, friend. NOW it gets the big order.
In the same way, Paul says, the women must be dignified, temperate and faithful in all things.

cards.question: In the middle of his lines about deacons, Paul also speaks about the women. What does he say the women must not be?
Back to deacons. Just like an overseer, a deacon must be the husband of but one wife.

cards.text: A deacon must also be a good manager of his children and his own household. And Paul says those who serve well as deacons walk away with something.

cards.question: What do those who serve well as deacons gain for themselves?

answers.text: High standing and great confidence in the faith
A larger share of the church's offerings
A seat among the overseers of the church

cards.text: Paul hopes to come to Timothy soon, but he's writing these things in case he's delayed. Friend, we've all sent a "running late" text, but Paul sent instructions for the whole CHURCH.

cards.question: Why is Paul writing all this down for Timothy?

answers.text: So he knows how people must act in God's household
So he can read it aloud to the city's rulers
So he can choose who will take Paul's place

cards.text: And what is God's household? Paul says it's the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
Then Paul ends BIG. By common confession, he says, the mystery of godliness is great: "He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels" and he's not done yet.

cards.question: Paul calls it the mystery of godliness, the confession about the One who appeared in the flesh. Paul says the news about Him stayed a secret shared by only a few.
Paul's list starts with Him appearing in the flesh. Where does the list end?

answers.text: He was taken up in glory
He was laid in a tomb

findings.problem: The second sentence says that Paul likewise does not give deacons the job until they have proven themselves. That already retells the testing-before-service movement of verse 10, so citing only verse 9 is narrower than what the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Verse 16's movements “was proclaimed among the nations” and “was believed in throughout the world” are never told or positively asked. Learning only that the news was not a secret shared by a few does not give the baker those two important parts of the confession.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: “Him” and “the list” have no antecedent within the question and depend on remembering earlier cards. The question should identify whose confession or list it is, such as the One who appeared in the flesh, so it stands alone.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
